title: The Chess Player
text: A figure in a hood sits at a stone table with a board set out, the pieces carved from teeth. Its hands are very long and very still. If it wins, it says, it takes one of you, and there are already a great many pieces in its box. If you win, it gives you the board.

options.label: The wisest sits down to play for their life.

outcomes.text: Checkmate. It bows, slowly, and the board of teeth is yours.
Checkmate. It reaches across the board and takes a little of them, and puts it in the box.
It sees, and laughs, a long dry laugh, and sweeps the board clean, and lets you go.
It shrugs and sets the pieces up again. The Leader finds themself playing the game in their head all day, and cannot stop, and grows sharper for it.

options.label: The Tinkerer studies how the pieces move.

outcomes.text: The pieces are clockwork, and the Tinkerer sees the trick in them. Nine moves, and the board is theirs.
The pieces are clockwork, and so, the Tinkerer sees too late, is the player. It takes a finger for the insult.
